identity.title: The ALMA Frontier Fields Survey. VI. Lensing-corrected 1.1 mm number counts in Abell 2744, MACSJ0416.1-2403, MACSJ1149.5+2223, Abell 370, and Abell S1063

paper_type_evidence.quote: We aim to derive number counts at $1.1\,\textmd{mm}$ down to flux densities fainter than $0.1\,\textmd{mJy}$, based on ALMA observations towards five *Hubble* Frontier Fields (FF) galaxy clusters, following a statistical approach to correct for lensing effects.
Five out of the six FF galaxy clusters were observed by ALMA in Band 6, as part of the ALMA Frontier Fields Survey (programs #2013.1.00999.S in cycle 2 and #2015.1.01425.S in cycle 3, PI: F. Bauer).

question.value: Derive lensing-corrected 1.1 mm number counts down to flux densities fainter than 0.1 mJy towards five Hubble Frontier Fields galaxy clusters and determine their contribution to the extragalactic background light (EBL).

evidence.quote: We aim to derive number counts at $1.1\,\textmd{mm}$ down to flux densities fainter than $0.1\,\textmd{mJy}$, based on ALMA observations towards five *Hubble* Frontier Fields (FF) galaxy clusters, following a statistical approach to correct for lensing effects.

We find a median contribution to the extragalactic background light (EBL) of $14_{-8}^{+12}\,\textmd{Jy}\,\textmd{deg}^{-2}$ resolved in our demagnified sources down to $\approx0.01\,\textmd{mJy}$, representing $75-86\%$ of Planck-derived extragalactic EBL estimates at $1.1\,\textmd{mm}$.
Five out of the six FF galaxy clusters were observed by ALMA in Band 6, as part of the ALMA Frontier Fields Survey (programs #2013.1.00999.S in cycle 2 and #2015.1.01425.S in cycle 3, PI: F. Bauer).

frequencies_and_spectral_setup.value: Local Oscillator frequency 263.14 GHz (~1.1 mm), 126 pointings per cluster covering ~2' x 2'

evidence.quote: For the five clusters, the inner $\approx2'\times2'$ FF regions were covered with 126 pointings each, with a Local Oscillator frequency set to $263.14\,\textmd{GHz}$ ($\approx1.1\,\textmd{mm}$).

ALMA 1.1mm mosaics used for our source extraction covered the inner $\approx2'\times2'$ FF regions, reached rms depths of $\approx55-71\,\mu\textmd{Jy}\,\textmd{beam}^{-1}$, and had synthesized beam sizes between $\approx0.5\ensuremath{''}-1.5\ensuremath{''}$ (natural weighting).

analysis_steps.goal: Source detection and extraction in ALMA 1.1 mm mosaics

method.value: Search for pixels with S/N >= 4.5 within the PB > 0.3 region and group pixels into individual sources using the DBSCAN algorithm.

evidence.quote: We detect sources by searching for pixels with signal-to-noise ratio $(\textmd{S/N})$ larger or equal than a given threshold, grouping pixels as individual sources with the DBSCAN python algorithm (cite: Pedregosa2012).
Therefore, in this study we use $\textmd{PB}>0.3$ for all cluster fields.

We choose a threshold of $\textmd{S/N}=4.5$, as this is found to be an appropriate tradeoff between the purity and completeness correction factors that will be applied to our number counts (see $\S$[3](#sect_method)).
Therefore, in this study we use $\textmd{PB}>0.3$ for all cluster fields.

validation.value: Checked spurious detections in negative mosaics and 300 simulated noise maps

evidence.quote: This is consistent within $1\sigma$ with both the amount of spurious sources from the negative mosaics (zero and one, respectively) and the number of sources without reliable counterparts at other wavelengths (two and one, respectively).

analysis_steps.goal: Measure integrated flux densities and sizes of detected sources

method.value: For high-significance (S/N >= 5) sources, fit elliptical Gaussians in the uv-plane using UVMCMCFIT. For low-significance (4.5 <= S/N < 5) sources, scale peak intensities using median size parameters from high-S/N sources and source injection simulations.

evidence.quote: We measure integrated flux densities in the *uv*-plane for our new high-significance detections as in Paper I, using the UVMCMCFIT python algorithm (cite: Bussmann2016).

As in Paper IV, we estimate the integrated flux densities of low-significance detections in A370 and AS1063 using source peak intensities; this choice is motivated by the large uncertainties in integrated source flux densities that are given at low S/N by two-dimensional Gaussian fits in the $uv$-plane.

key_parameters.value: Peak-to-integrated flux ratios of 0.80 (A370) and 0.71 (AS1063) for 4.5 <= S/N < 5 sources

evidence.quote: We conduct source injection simulations (see $\S$[3](#sect_method)), finding a typical ratio between the peak and integrated flux density for these size parameters of 0.80 and 0.71 in A370 and AS1063, respectively.

assumptions.value: Low-significance detections have observed effective radius r_eff,obs = 0.23'' and axial ratio q_obs = 0.58 (median of high-S/N sources)

evidence.quote: We adopt as their observed effective radius and axial ratio the median values found for the high-significance sources. Including the five FFs, these are $r_{\textmd{eff,obs}}=0.23\ensuremath{''}$ and $q_{\textmd{obs}}=0.58$, respectively.

evidence.quote: Since we have assumed a given image-plane source size for low-significance detections (11/29 of our sample), we explore the effect of varying this source size by testing two extreme cases.

method.value: Cross-match ALMA detections with spectroscopic (ALMA linescan, GLASS, VLT/MUSE, Gemini/GMOS) and photometric (HFF-DeepSpace EAZY posteriors, Paper II) catalogs; assign Gaussian redshift prior to unassociated sources.

evidence.quote: When available, we use spectroscopic redshifts and (if not) photometric redshift probability distributions.

Nine detections have no reliable counterparts in the aforementioned catalogs. As in Paper IV, for these sources we assume a Gaussian redshift distribution centered at $z=2$ with $\sigma=0.5$, which is consistent within $1\sigma$ with average redshift values found for faint dusty galaxies from the literature (e.g. (cite: Aravena2016; Dunlop2017; Aravena2020)).

key_parameters.value: Matching radius <= 0.5'' for photometric counterparts (up to ~1'' for spectroscopic), redshift quality parameter p_Delta_z ~ 1

evidence.quote: Among the sources that lack spectroscopic redshifts, one in A370 and two in AS1063 have counterparts with reliable photometric redshifts within $0.5\ensuremath{''}$. We use the redshift quality parameter $p_{\Delta z}$ provided by the catalog as a measure of the $z_{\textmd{phot}}$ reliability, with $p_{\Delta z}\approx1$ indicating that most of the total integrated probability lies within $\Delta z=0.2$ of the $z_{\textmd{phot}}$ estimate.

assumptions.value: Gaussian redshift distribution z = 2 +/- 0.5 for sources without counterparts

evidence.quote: As in Paper IV, for these sources we assume a Gaussian redshift distribution centered at $z=2$ with $\sigma=0.5$, which is consistent within $1\sigma$ with average redshift values found for faint dusty galaxies from the literature (e.g. (cite: Aravena2016; Dunlop2017; Aravena2020)).

validation.value: Tested four alternative redshift distribution assumptions across all detections (Gaussian z=2+/-0.5, fixed z=2, uniform from cluster z to 4, Gaussian z=3+/-0.5)

evidence.quote: As in Paper IV, we explore the effect of adopting different source redshifts in the predicted counts, considering the following cases for all detections: a) assuming a Gaussian redshift distribution centered at $z=2\pm0.5$, b) adopting exactly $z=2$, c) assuming a uniform redshift distribution between the cluster redshift and $z=4$, and d) assuming a Gaussian redshift distribution centered at $z=3\pm0.5$.

validation.value: Compared simulated noise map spurious counts with negative mosaic detections and unassociated source counts

evidence.quote: Based on the source extraction on the simulated noise maps, the average number of spurious sources at $\textmd{S/N}\geq4.5$ is $0.93\pm1.33$ for A370 and $1.45\pm1.79$ for AS1063. analysis_steps.goal: Compute source-plane magnification maps and effective areas from lens models

method.value: Reproject surface mass density and shear maps from public v4/v4.1 lens models to ALMA resolution, deflect magnification and PB-corrected rms maps to the source plane over a redshift grid, and integrate pixels where S_demag,peak / sigma_demag >= 4.5.

evidence.quote: We use the full set of individual mass reconstructions released by the teams (which sample the range of uncertainties), reprojected to the size and resolution of the ALMA maps.

At each demagnified peak intensity $S_{\textmd{demag,peak}}$, the effective area $A_{\textmd{eff}}$ is obtained from the source-plane pixels that satisfy $S_{\textmd{demag,peak}}/\sigma_{\textmd{demag}}\geq4.5$, with $\sigma_{\textmd{demag}}$ the PB-corrected rms corrected for magnification.

Since we need to create several source-plane maps for each lens model (sampling the source redshift distributions) but also want our Monte Carlo simulations to run fast, we precompute source-plane maps for all mass reconstructions and lens models, over the redshift range $z_{\textmd{min}}=0.4$ to $z_{\textmd{max}}=4$, using steps of $\Delta z=0.2$.

key_parameters.value: Redshift grid z_min = 0.4 to z_max = 4 with step Delta z = 0.2; 8, 9, 7, 9, and 9 lens models for A2744, MACSJ0416, MACSJ1149, A370, and AS1063

evidence.quote: Table [\[tab_models\]](#tab_models) lists these models, together with the models considered for the two FF clusters introduced in this work; we adopt for use eight, nine, seven, nine, and nine lens models for A2744, MACSJ0416, MACSJ1149, A370, and AS1063, respectively.

assumptions.value: No magnification (mu = 1) for pixels missing in lens model maps; neglect differential magnification; flat LambdaCDM cosmology with H_0 = 70 km s^-1 Mpc^-1, Omega_m = 0.3, Omega_Lambda = 0.7

evidence.quote: We adopt a flat $\Lambda$CDM cosmology with parameters $H_0=70\,\textmd{km}\,\textmd{s}^{-1}\textmd{Mpc}^{-1}$, $\Omega_m=0.3$ and $\Omega_{\Lambda}=0.7$.
We consider no magnification effects ($\mu=1$) for the missing pixels in magnification maps.

We neglect the effects of differential magnification, as all our detections lie far enough (i.e. more than four synthesized beams away) from critical lines in most of the adopted redshifts and lens models[^5].

validation.value: Compared results across all independent v4/v4.1 lens models

evidence.quote: We find variations across lens models in the median differential counts per flux bin up to $\approx0.6\,\textmd{dex}$ (although consistent within the error bars).

analysis_steps.goal: Derive lensing-corrected differential and cumulative number counts via Monte Carlo simulations

method.value: Run 1000 Monte Carlo realizations per lens model per cluster drawing observed fluxes, peak intensities, redshifts, and lens mass reconstructions, computing demagnified fluxes and summing weights X_i = (1 - p_false,i) / (C_i * A_eff,i). Combine by taking medians and adding 16th/84th percentile errors in quadrature with Gehrels Poisson uncertainties.

evidence.quote: We run 1000 realizations of the number counts per lens model per cluster field.
X_i=\frac{1-p_{\textmd{false},i}}{C_i\,A_{\textmd{eff},i}}.

We finally obtain combined differential (cumulative) counts, both in each separate cluster and including the five FFs, as the median values per flux density bin (limit). The associated uncertainties are given by the 16th and 84th percentiles, added in quadrature with scaled Poisson confidence levels for $1\sigma$ lower and upper limits (cite: Gehrels1986).

key_parameters.value: 1000 realizations per lens model per cluster field

evidence.quote: We run 1000 realizations of the number counts per lens model per cluster field.

assumptions.value: Modified black body with beta = 1.5, T_dust = 35 K, z = 2.5 when scaling literature counts from 850 um, 1.2 mm, and 1.3 mm to 1.1 mm

evidence.quote: Since we include in our comparison counts derived at wavelengths other than $1.1\,\textmd{mm}$, we scale their estimates as $S_{1.1\,\textmd{mm}}=1.59\times S_{1.3\,\textmd{mm}}$, $S_{1.1\,\textmd{mm}}=1.27\times S_{1.2\,\textmd{mm}}$, and $S_{1.1\,\textmd{mm}}=0.51\times S_{850\,\mu\textmd{m}}$. These factors are obtained assuming a modified black body model with a dust emissivity index $\beta=1.5$, dust temperature $T_{\textmd{dust}}=35\,\textmd{K}$, and $z=2.5$, which are values typically found for dusty galaxies (e.g. (cite: Swinbank2014)).

analysis_steps.goal: Compute resolved and extrapolated Extragalactic Background Light (EBL) at 1.1 mm

method.value: Sum the integrated flux contribution across differential count bins in each Monte Carlo realization, and fit a double power-law function to non-zero bins of each realization to integrate down to S_lim = 0, 0.013, and 0.133 mJy.

evidence.quote: Using the Monte Carlo realizations of our differential number counts, we compute the contribution to the extragalactic background light (EBL) provided by each of them, by adding up the contribution contained in each flux bin.
In order to estimate the EBL derived from our counts at $1.1\,\textmd{mm}$ for any flux density limit, we fit a double power-law function (e.g., (cite: Scott2002)) to our differential number counts.

results_numeric.quantity: Empirical field-to-field cosmic variance down to 0.013 mJy

evidence.quote: First, we derive the field-to-field variance directly from our cumulative counts, computing the variance from the median counts per cluster field down to $0.013\,\textmd{mJy}$. Dividing its square root by the number of clusters and the corresponding median combined counts, we obtain a relative uncertainty of 17%.

evidence.quote: We find a median contribution of $14.3_{-7.4}^{+12.2}$ ($7.5_{-3.9}^{+6.4}$) $\textmd{Jy}\,\textmd{deg}^{-2}$ resolved in our demagnified sources at $1.1\,\textmd{mm}$ down to $0.013$ ($0.133$) $\textmd{mJy}$; here, uncertainties are computed from the 16th and 84th percentiles.

evidence.quote: From these fits, we find median parameters and associated uncertainties (from 16th and 84th percentiles) of $N_0=2.7_{-1.7}^{+5.0}\times10^5\,\textmd{mJy}\,\textmd{deg}^{-2}$, $S_0=3.6_{-2.3}^{+2.5}\times10^{-2}\,\textmd{mJy}$, $\alpha=2.8_{-0.8}^{+1.0}$, and $\beta=0.6_{-1.6}^{+0.4}$.

findings_qualitative.value: Cumulative 1.1 mm number counts flatten below ~0.1 mJy and extend down to ~0.01 mJy, consistent within 1 sigma with Paper IV and the ASPECS-LP survey.

evidence.quote: Importantly, the flattening found for our cumulative counts at $\lesssim0.1\,\textmd{mJy}$ also extends further to $\approx0.01\,\textmd{mJy}$, i.e., $\approx0.4\,\textmd{dex}$ fainter than ASPECS-LP, and remains in agreement with extrapolations of their number counts down to this flux limit.

findings_qualitative.value: Cosmic variance estimates (9-31%) are exceeded by Monte Carlo simulation uncertainties (75-281%) and Poisson uncertainties (48-79%) at the faintest flux limit.

evidence.quote: At our faintest flux limit, uncertainties in the median combined cumulative counts coming from our Monte Carlo simulations are in the range 75-281%, while those from Poisson statistics are in the range 48-79%. From these we note that cosmic variance estimates from the three approaches mentioned before are all exceeded by these uncertainties.

findings_qualitative.value: Most (75-86% compared to Planck/COBE, or ~94% of the double power-law total) of the 1.1 mm extragalactic background light is resolved by demagnified sources down to ~0.013 mJy.

evidence.quote: The contribution provided by our demagnified sources at $1.1\,\textmd{mm}$ down to $0.013$ ($0.133$) $\textmd{mJy}$ represents $74.5_{-38.4}^{+64.0}\%$ ($38.9_{-20.1}^{+33.9}\%$) of the EBL by (cite: Ade2014) and $86.4_{-50.0}^{+120.4}\%$ ($45.6_{-26.2}^{+57.3}\%$) of that by (cite: Odegard2019).

For $S_{\textmd{lim}}=0.013$ ($0.133$) $\textmd{mJy}$, we obtain a median contribution of $18.8_{-8.8}^{+40.4}$ ($5.0_{-3.1}^{+42.1}$) $\textmd{Jy}\,\textmd{deg}^{-2}$, corresponding to $94.2_{-14.8}^{+5.3}\%$ ($27.3_{-17.0}^{+63.0}\%$) of our estimate of the total EBL.

claims.hypothesis: Cumulative 1.1 mm number counts exhibit a flattening below ~0.1 mJy that persists when expanding the ALMA Frontier Fields sample to five galaxy clusters.
claims.experiment: Extracted 29 ALMA 1.1 mm continuum sources (S/N >= 4.5, PB > 0.3) across five FF clusters and derived lensing-corrected number counts via Monte Carlo simulations across multiple public v4/v4.1 lens models.
claims.result: Cumulative number counts below ~0.1 mJy are lower by ~0.4 dex compared to Fujimoto et al. (2016) and ASPECS-Pilot, agree within 1 sigma with Paper IV and ASPECS-LP, and have a double power-law turnover at S_0 = 3.6(+2.5/-2.3) x 10^-2 mJy.
claims.finding: The flattening of the 1.1 mm number counts below ~0.1 mJy down to ~0.01 mJy is confirmed and consistent with the knee of the high-redshift infrared luminosity function modeled by Popping et al. (2020).

evidence.quote: However, below $\approx0.1\,\textmd{mJy}$, our cumulative number counts are lower by $\approx0.4\,\textmd{dex}$ compared to two deep ALMA studies (namely one that probes several blank fields plus one lensed galaxy cluster, and the initial ALMA Spectroscopic Survey in the Hubble Ultra Deep Field, ASPECS-Pilot), while remaining consistent with the ASPECS Large Program (ASPECS-LP) within $1\sigma$.

In line with results from Paper IV, our findings continue suggesting a flattening in the number counts below $\approx0.1\,\textmd{mJy}$. This flux density is consistent within $\approx2.6\sigma$ with the parameterisation we found in $\S$[4.5](#sect_ebl) ($S_0=3.6_{-2.3}^{+2.5}\times10^{-2}\,\textmd{mJy}$).

claims.hypothesis: Uncertainties at the faint end of lensing-corrected number counts are dominated by lensing model and effective area uncertainties rather than cosmic variance or Poisson statistics.
claims.experiment: Compared Monte Carlo simulation uncertainties and Gehrels Poisson errors at the faintest flux limits against three independent cosmic variance estimates and across different lens models.
claims.result: At 0.013 mJy, Monte Carlo uncertainties are 75-281% and Poisson errors are 48-79%, whereas cosmic variance estimates are 9-31%; median differential counts vary by up to ~0.6 dex across lens models.
claims.finding: Cosmic variance is subdominant to Monte Carlo and Poisson uncertainties, and source-plane effective area uncertainties driven by magnification and intensity errors dominate the faint-end count uncertainties.

evidence.quote: At $0.13\,\textmd{mJy}$ and below, Monte Carlo simulation-based uncertainties dominate the combined cumulative counts over Poisson errors.

At our faintest flux limit, uncertainties in the median combined cumulative counts coming from our Monte Carlo simulations are in the range 75-281%, while those from Poisson statistics are in the range 48-79%. From these we note that cosmic variance estimates from the three approaches mentioned before are all exceeded by these uncertainties.

claims.hypothesis: Dusty star-forming galaxies down to ~0.01 mJy resolve the majority of the extragalactic background light (EBL) at 1.1 mm.
claims.experiment: Integrated the differential number counts from Monte Carlo realizations directly and via double power-law fits down to 0.013 mJy and compared with Planck and COBE/FIRAS EBL measurements at 263.14 GHz.
claims.result: Direct integration yields 14.3(+12.2/-7.4) Jy deg^-2 (74.5% of Planck and 86.4% of Odegard et al. 2019 EBL), and double power-law integration yields 18.8(+40.4/-8.8) Jy deg^-2 (94.2% of the total fitted EBL of 21.2 Jy deg^-2).
claims.finding: Most of the 1.1 mm EBL is resolved by galaxies down to ~0.013 mJy.

evidence.quote: The contribution provided by our demagnified sources at $1.1\,\textmd{mm}$ down to $0.013$ ($0.133$) $\textmd{mJy}$ represents $74.5_{-38.4}^{+64.0}\%$ ($38.9_{-20.1}^{+33.9}\%$) of the EBL by (cite: Ade2014) and $86.4_{-50.0}^{+120.4}\%$ ($45.6_{-26.2}^{+57.3}\%$) of that by (cite: Odegard2019).

For $S_{\textmd{lim}}=0.013$ ($0.133$) $\textmd{mJy}$, we obtain a median contribution of $18.8_{-8.8}^{+40.4}$ ($5.0_{-3.1}^{+42.1}$) $\textmd{Jy}\,\textmd{deg}^{-2}$, corresponding to $94.2_{-14.8}^{+5.3}\%$ ($27.3_{-17.0}^{+63.0}\%$) of our estimate of the total EBL. This suggests that we may be resolving most of the EBL at $1.1\,\textmd{mm}$ down to $0.013\,\textmd{mJy}$.

why_this_data.value: Strong gravitational lensing by the Frontier Fields massive galaxy clusters magnifies background sources beyond the confusion limit, and the fields have rich public multiwavelength data and multiple independent mass models. MACSJ0717.5+3745 was excluded because it was only partially observed to much lower sensitivity.

evidence.quote: This ALMA survey benefits from the unique ALMA capabilities and the strong gravitational lensing power of massive galaxy clusters, allowing to detect (if magnified) sources beyond the confusion limit (e.g., rms depths in the order of tens of $\mu\textmd{Jy}\,\textmd{beam}^{-1}$ for current deep ALMA maps at $1.1\,\textmd{mm}$).
Since the sixth FF cluster, MACSJ0717.5+3745, was only partially observed in cycle 3 to much lower sensitivity, source extraction was not performed on it, and thus we do not include it in this study.

why_this_method.value: Monte Carlo simulations fold uncertainties from observed flux densities, redshift distributions, and multiple lens models into the number counts. S/N = 4.5 was chosen as a tradeoff between purity and completeness, PB > 0.3 was chosen to include a high-S/N detection (A370-ID02 at PB = 0.34), and peak intensity scaling was used for 4.5 <= S/N < 5 sources because uv-plane Gaussian fits have large uncertainties at low S/N.

evidence.quote: We choose a threshold of $\textmd{S/N}=4.5$, as this is found to be an appropriate tradeoff between the purity and completeness correction factors that will be applied to our number counts (see $\S$[3](#sect_method)).
However, in one of the last two FFs we find a high $\textmd{S/N}$ source at $\textmd{PB}=0.34$, A370-ID02. Therefore, in this study we use $\textmd{PB}>0.3$ for all cluster fields.

As in Paper IV, we estimate the integrated flux densities of low-significance detections in A370 and AS1063 using source peak intensities; this choice is motivated by the large uncertainties in integrated source flux densities that are given at low S/N by two-dimensional Gaussian fits in the $uv$-plane.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Zitrin & Merten v3 lens models were rejected because only v4 or newer models (which use the best data to date as constraints) were considered; GLAFIC v4 was excluded for A370 because it did not cover A370-ID03.

evidence.quote: We consider only v4 or newer models, as these use the best data to date as constraints[^4]. We also restrict our set only to models that cover the whole region where our ALMA sources lie. A370-ID03 is not covered by GLAFIC v4 model, and therefore we do not include it for A370.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Photometric redshift for AS1063-ID05 (z_phot = 2.256) was rejected because its quality parameter p_Delta_z ~ 0.2 indicated a broad/multi-modal distribution; Herschel IR redshift (~0.9) for A370-ID03 was rejected in favor of its spectroscopic redshift.

evidence.quote: AS1063-ID05 has a counterpart within $\approx0.3\ensuremath{''}$ having $z_{\textmd{phot}}=2.256_{-1.302}^{+1.766}$. However, it has $p_{\Delta z}\approx0.2$, indicating a broad and/or multi-modal probability distribution. Therefore, we do not include this redshift estimate in this work.

A370-ID03 has a IR-estimated redshift of $\sim0.9$ from SED fitting using five *Herschel* bands (see (cite: Rawle2016)); we do not use this estimate, as we prioritize the spectroscopic redshift found for A370-ID03.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Separate Eddington bias corrections were skipped because flux enhancements from SIDES simulations were consistent with image-plane deboosting corrections.

evidence.quote: These ratios are consistent with the deboosting corrections obtained in Fig. [3](#fig_debcorr). We thus consider safe to skip Eddington bias corrections in this work.

how_they_decided_enough.value: Counts are presented down to 0.024 mJy because it is the faintest bin where at least one cluster has non-zero combined differential counts at the 84th percentile; redshift grids were precomputed with Delta z = 0.2 to keep the 1000 Monte Carlo realizations per model fast.

evidence.quote: Since we need to create several source-plane maps for each lens model (sampling the source redshift distributions) but also want our Monte Carlo simulations to run fast, we precompute source-plane maps for all mass reconstructions and lens models, over the redshift range $z_{\textmd{min}}=0.4$ to $z_{\textmd{max}}=4$, using steps of $\Delta z=0.2$.

We present counts down to the flux density bin centered on $0.024\,\textmd{mJy}$, as this is the faintest flux density bin where at least one cluster field has non-zero combined differential counts at the 84th percentile.

limitations_admitted.value: Nine out of 29 ALMA detections (and all but one of the faint-end contributors) lack reliable multiwavelength counterparts, requiring an assumed Gaussian redshift distribution (z = 2 +/- 0.5) and preventing detailed physical comparison with models.

evidence.quote: Nine detections have no reliable counterparts in the aforementioned catalogs. As in Paper IV, for these sources we assume a Gaussian redshift distribution centered at $z=2$ with $\sigma=0.5$, which is consistent within $1\sigma$ with average redshift values found for faint dusty galaxies from the literature (e.g. (cite: Aravena2016; Dunlop2017; Aravena2020)).

Moreover, only one of the sources that contribute to our faint-end number counts has a reliable counterpart (AS1063-ID04, see Table [\[tab_snr45gals\]](#tab_snr45gals) and Fig. [6](#fig_flux_intr_flux_obs)), preventing a detailed comparison with (cite: Popping2020) results.

limitations_admitted.value: Some lens models (GLAFIC v4, Sharon v4, Williams v4/v4.1) do not fully cover the PB > 0.3 region (missing 0.7% to 19% of the area), where no magnification (mu = 1) had to be assumed.

evidence.quote: A fraction of the region where the ALMA maps have $\textmd{PB}>0.3$ is not fully covered by the models GLAFIC v4 ($\sim2\%$ and $3\%$ for A2744 and AS1063, respectively), Sharon v4 ($\sim0.7\%$ for A370), Williams v4 ($\sim3\%$, $19\%$, $10\%$ and $14\%$ for A2744, MACSJ0416, MACSJ1149 and A370, respectively) and Williams v4.1 ($\sim14\%$ for A370). We consider no magnification effects ($\mu=1$) for the missing pixels in magnification maps.

limitations_admitted.value: Systematic discrepancies across different lens models reach up to ~0.6 dex in median differential counts, and for most sources model-to-model magnification discrepancies exceed individual model uncertainties.

evidence.quote: For most sources, the discrepancies in the median values predicted by different models exceed their individual uncertainties, as Fig. [5](#fig_magnif_gal) shows.
We find variations across lens models in the median differential counts per flux bin up to $\approx0.6\,\textmd{dex}$ (although consistent within the error bars).

limitations_admitted.value: The bright end of the number counts (> 1 mJy) is expected to be affected by cosmic variance due to the small survey area, missing massive (> 10^11 M_sun) bright galaxies.

evidence.quote: Therefore, from their estimates we expect the bright end of our number counts ($>1\,\textmd{mJy}$) to be more affected by cosmic variance, missing a fraction of the objects with stellar mass in the range $5\times10^{10}-10^{11}\,\textmd{M}_{\odot}$ and most of the objects at $>10^{11}\,\textmd{M}_{\odot}$ that a wider-area survey may detect.

referee_caveats_inferred: Low-significance detections (4.5 <= S/N < 5) make up 11/29 of the catalog (including almost all of the faintest demagnified sources), have a high expected spurious fraction (18-28% at S/N >= 4.5), lack multiwavelength counterparts (9/11), and rely on assumed source sizes and redshifts.
Cycle 5 ALMA spectroscopic redshifts for 5 sources in A2744 are taken from an unpublished work in preparation (Bauer et al., in prep.) without showing spectra.
Differential magnification effects are neglected even though dust continuum sizes (r_eff ~ 0.23'') are extended.

data_public_as_stated.value: Public lens models obtained from MAST (http://archive.stsci.edu/prepds/frontier/lensmodels/) and photometric redshift distributions from HFF-DeepSpace; ALMA project codes are listed.

evidence.quote: We correct our number counts by gravitational lensing effects making use of the models publicly available in the FF website[^2], which are produced by independent teams.
The ALMA observations were carried out under programs ADS/JAO.ALMA#2013.1.00999.S, ADS/JAO.ALMA#2015.1.01425.S, and ADS/JAO.ALMA#2017.1.01219.S.
The lens models were obtained from the Mikulski Archive for Space Telescopes (MAST).

DBSCAN clustering parameters (eps, min_samples) used for source extraction

reproducibility.estimated_data_volume_inferred: Moderate (~50-200 GB for raw visibility data across five 126-pointing Band 6 mosaics, or ~5-10 GB for reduced continuum mosaics and public MAST lens model FITS maps)
reproducibility.score_reason: The ALMA project codes, public MAST lens model versions, source catalog (positions, peak and uv-fitted fluxes, sizes, and redshifts), and final number count tables are thoroughly documented. However, full end-to-end reproduction requires custom Monte Carlo lensing simulation scripts that are not released, reduction details deferred to Paper I/III/IV, and unstated DBSCAN and noise-simulation parameters.
reproducibility.rediscovery_reason: All ALMA datasets (2013.1.00999.S, 2015.1.01425.S, 2017.1.01219.S) and MAST Frontier Fields lens models are public, and the main results (source catalog fluxes/sizes, lensing-corrected differential/cumulative number counts, and EBL contributions) are concrete numeric benchmarks.
